grammar.intro:
Croatian modal verbs are always followed by the **infinitive** of the main verb. The five main modals are:
- **moći** — can / to be able to
- **smjeti** — may / to be allowed to
- **morati** — must / to have to
- **trebati** — to need / should
- **htjeti** — to want

Key distinction: **ne smijem** = I must not (prohibition — it is forbidden); **ne moram** = I don't have to (no obligation — it is not required)

rules.label: moći — can / to be able to
rules.explanation:
Use **moći** to express ability or possibility. Conjugation: **mogu / možeš / može / možemo / možete / mogu**.

For polite requests, use **'Mogu li...?'** (Can I...?) or **'Možeš li...?'** (Can you...?).

rules.label: smjeti and morati — permission and obligation
rules.explanation:
Use **smjeti** for permission: **smijem / smiješ / smije / smijemo / smijete / smiju**.
Use **morati** for obligation: **moram / moraš / mora / moramo / morate / moraju**.

Critical difference in the negative:
- **Ne smijem ući.** = I must not enter. (it is forbidden)
- **Ne moram ići.** = I don't have to go. (it is not required)

examples.en: Are we allowed to come in?

rules.label: trebati and htjeti — need/should and want
rules.explanation:
Use **trebati** for need or mild obligation: **trebam / trebaš / treba / trebamo / trebate / trebaju**.
Impersonal form: **'Treba mi...'** = I need... (literally 'it is needed by me').

Use **htjeti** for want — long forms **hoću / hoćeš / hoće / hoćemo / hoćete / hoće**, short forms **ću / ćeš / će / ćemo / ćete / će** (also used for the future tense).

paragraphs.hr: Ana mora pakirati kofere jer odlazi sutra ujutro, ali želi još jednom popiti kavu s Markom.
paragraphs.en: Ana must pack her suitcases because she is leaving tomorrow morning, but she wants to have one last coffee with Marko.

paragraphs.hr: „Možeš li doći sada?" pita Ana Marka telefonom. „Ne moram otići do podneva."
paragraphs.en: "Can you come now?" Ana asks Marko on the phone. "I don't have to leave until noon."

paragraphs.hr: Marko dolazi i Ana kaže: „Ne mogu naći svoju putovnicu! Svuda sam tražila."
paragraphs.en: Marko arrives and Ana says: "I can't find my passport! I've looked everywhere."

paragraphs.hr: „Ne smiješ kasniti na let," kaže Marko. „Treba ti više vremena za traženje."
paragraphs.en: "You must not be late for the flight," says Marko. "You need more time to search."

paragraphs.hr: Dok piju kavu, razgovaraju o sljedećem posjetu. „Trebala bi posjetiti Dubrovnik i Plitvička jezera," kaže Marko.
paragraphs.en: While drinking coffee, they talk about the next visit. "You should visit Dubrovnik and Plitvice Lakes," says Marko.

paragraphs.hr: „Hoću doći opet sljedeće ljeto," obećava Ana. „Ne mogu zamisliti da ne vidim Hrvatsku opet!"
paragraphs.en: "I want to come again next summer," Ana promises. "I can't imagine not seeing Croatia again!"

readingQuestions.prompt: Why must Ana pack her suitcases?
options: She is going to a party tonight.
readingQuestions.explanation: Ana 'mora pakirati kofere jer odlazi sutra ujutro' — she must pack because she is leaving tomorrow morning.
Ana says 'Ne mogu naći svoju putovnicu' — I can't find my passport.

readingQuestions.prompt: Until what time does Ana NOT have to leave?
readingQuestions.explanation: Ana says 'Ne moram otići do podneva' — I don't have to leave until noon.

readingQuestions.prompt: What does Marko say Ana should visit on her next trip?
readingQuestions.explanation: Marko says 'Trebala bi posjetiti Dubrovnik i Plitvička jezera'.

readingQuestions.prompt: What does Ana promise at the end of the story?
options: She will come again next summer.
She will call Marko every day.
readingQuestions.explanation: Ana says 'Hoću doći opet sljedeće ljeto' — I want to come again next summer.

test.prompt: What does 'mogu' mean?
What is the correct form of 'morati' for 'you (sg.) must'?
Which form means 'she may / she is allowed to'?
What is the correct form of 'trebati' for 'we need/should'?
What does 'hoće' mean (3rd person singular/plural of 'htjeti')?
How do you say 'I must not' (something is forbidden)?
test.explanation: 'Ne smijem' = I must not (prohibition). 'Ne moram' = I don't have to (no obligation).

test.prompt: How do you say 'I don't have to' (it is not required)?
test.explanation: 'Ne moram' = I don't have to (no obligation). 'Ne smijem' = I must not (prohibition).

test.prompt: Choose the correct translation: 'She can speak Croatian.'
Fill in: 'Ne ___ pušiti ovdje.' (You must not smoke here — it is forbidden.)
test.explanation: 'Ne smiješ' = you must not (it is forbidden). Use 'smjeti' for prohibition.

test.prompt: What does 'Treba mi...' mean?
test.explanation: 'Treba mi' is an impersonal construction meaning 'I need...' (literally 'it is needed by me').

test.prompt: What does 'hoću' mean?
Fill in: 'On ___ doći sutra.' (He must come tomorrow.)
What does 'Možeš li mi pomoći?' mean?
options: Do you want to help me?

test.prompt: How do you make a polite request starting with 'Can I...?' in Croatian?
test.explanation: 'Mogu li...?' (Can I...?) is the standard polite way to request permission or assistance.

test.prompt: What is the 1st person singular of 'smjeti'?
What does 'Ne moram ići' mean?
test.explanation: 'Ne moram' = I don't have to (no obligation). It does NOT mean 'I must not'.

test.prompt: What does 'Ne smijem ući' mean?
test.explanation: 'Ne smijem' = I must not (prohibition — it is forbidden).

test.prompt: Which sentence means 'She should study'?
test.explanation: 'Treba' (should/needs to) expresses mild obligation or advice. 'Može' = can, 'smije' = may, 'hoće' = wants to.

test.prompt: Translate: 'They can sing.'
What does 'Hoćeš li doći?' mean?
options: Will you / Do you want to come?
test.explanation: 'Hoćeš' = you want / you will. 'Hoćeš li doći?' = Will you come? / Do you want to come?

test.prompt: Translate: 'We must speak Croatian.'
Translate: 'I want to eat.'
Which sentence means 'You (plural) are allowed to enter'?
test.explanation: 'Smijete' is the 2nd person plural of 'smjeti' (to be allowed).

test.prompt: What does 'mora' express in 'Ona mora raditi'?
What kind of sentence is 'Mogu li koristiti tvoj telefon?'
test.explanation: 'Mogu li...?' (Can I...?) is the standard form for polite requests in Croatian.

items.note: 1st person singular — same form as 3rd person plural

items.en: I may / I am allowed to

items.note: NOT the same as 'I don't have to'
Long and short forms — short forms also make the future tense

items.en: Will you come? / Do you want to come?
